summary: A UV-enhanced atomic layer deposition (UV-ALD) process was developed to deposit ZrO2 thin films on PET substrates using zirconium tetra-tert-butoxide (Zr[OC(CH3)3]4) and H2O as precursors at room temperature. The UV light was effective in achieving high-quality ZrO2 thin films with good adhesive strength on polymer substrates.
evidence: A UV-enhanced atomic layer deposition (UV-ALD) process was developed to deposit ZrO2 thin films on poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) polymer substrates using zirconium tetra-tert-butoxide (ZTB) and H2O as precursors with UV light. The UV light was very effective to obtain the high-quality ZrO2 thin films with good adhesive strength on polymer substrates.
